# Object schemas

The object contracts of spec §28. A **nullable** field may be `null`, which means the value is unknown — never that it is zero or empty (spec §10.5). `identity` is what makes two observations of the same object the same object.

## ActionResult — `ono.action-result/1`

The outcome of one mutation against one target.

Identity: `target`, `operation`

Default view: `target`, `operation`, `status`, `changed`, `duration`

| field | type | unit | presence | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `target` | `value` | — | required | A reference to the object the operation acted on. Typed as a value because a mutation can act on any object kind; `inspect` resolves it back to the full record. |
| `operation` | `string` | — | required | The command id of the operation, e.g. `ono.service.restart`. |
| `status` | `enum` | — | required | The outcome. `skipped` is not a failure — it is the honest answer when the target was already in the requested state and nothing was done. |
| `changed` | `bool` | — | required | Whether the system state actually changed. A successful no-op is `success` and `false`. |
| `message` | `string` | — | nullable | A one-line human summary; null when the status says everything there is to say. |
| `error` | `ono.error/1` | — | nullable | The structured error for a failed result; null for `success` and `skipped`. |
| `duration` | `duration` | — | required | How long the operation took, so that a slow success is visible as such. |

## ConfigSetting — `ono.config-setting/1`

One resolved configuration setting together with the layer that set it.

Identity: `key`

Default view: `key`, `value`, `layer`, `source`

| field | type | unit | presence | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | `string` | — | required | The dotted setting key, e.g. `render.table.max_rows` (spec §30). |
| `value` | `value` | — | required | The resolved value, in its own type — `64MiB` is a bytesize, not the string "64MiB". Typed as a value because settings span the whole value model. |
| `type` | `string` | — | required | The declared type of the setting, so `explain` and completion can check an assignment. |
| `layer` | `enum` | — | required | Which of ADR-0010's five layers supplied the effective value; later layers override earlier ones. |
| `source` | `path` | — | nullable | The file that set it; null for the built-in default layer and for the environment and invocation layers, which have no file. |
| `line` | `int` | — | nullable | The line within `source`; null wherever `source` is null. |
| `default_value` | `value` | — | nullable | The built-in default, so the user can see what they have overridden. |
| `description` | `string` | — | nullable | One line describing what the setting does, shown by `help` and by completion. |

## Endpoint — `ono.endpoint/1`

One end of a socket: an address and port, or a filesystem path for a Unix socket.

Identity: 

Default view: `address`, `port`

| field | type | unit | presence | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `address` | `ip` | — | nullable | The IP address; null for a Unix-domain or unbound endpoint. |
| `port` | `port` | — | nullable | The transport port; null where the protocol has none. |
| `path` | `path` | — | nullable | The filesystem path of a Unix-domain socket; null for every other family. |
| `host` | `string` | — | nullable | The reverse-resolved host name. Null unless resolution was requested and succeeded; §22.2 classes it as derived, so it is never substituted for `address`. |

## EnvVar — `ono.env-var/1`

One environment or shell variable, as a record rather than a line of `NAME=value`.

Identity: `name`

Default view: `name`, `value`, `exported`

| field | type | unit | presence | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | — | required | The variable name. |
| `value` | `string` | — | required | The value, verbatim and unsplit. Never null: a variable that is not set does not produce a record at all, which is the distinction spec §10.5 insists on. |
| `exported` | `bool` | — | required | Whether the variable is part of the environment passed to child processes, as opposed to a shell-local binding (ADR-0009 `let`). |
| `source` | `enum` | — | required | Where the current value came from, so `get env` answers "who set this" the way `get config` does. |

## Error — `ono.error/1`

A structured error, carrying a stable code rather than a message to grep.

Identity: 

Default view: `code`, `name`, `message`, `target`

| field | type | unit | presence | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `code` | `string` | — | required | The stable code, rendered as spec §43 writes it, e.g. `Ono-Sendai-E0301`. |
| `name` | `string` | — | required | The dotted selector, e.g. `io.not_found`. This is what predicates and `catch` match on (ADR-0006); it is stable even when the human message improves. |
| `kind` | `enum` | — | required | The broad category scripts branch on. See `docs/spec/errors.yaml` and ADR-0006. |
| `message` | `string` | — | required | The human message. Terse by default, rich on demand (spec §16.2). |
| `target` | `value` | — | nullable | A reference to the object the error is about; null for errors that are about no object. |
| `source` | `ono.error/1` | — | nullable | The underlying cause, so a chain is inspectable rather than flattened into one string. |
| `help` | `string` | — | nullable | What the user should do about it; null when nothing useful can be said. |
| `retryable` | `bool` | — | nullable | Whether retrying the same operation could succeed. Null when unknown — which is different from `false`, and spec §10.5 requires the difference to survive. |
| `span` | `record` | — | nullable | The byte range of the source text the error refers to, for parse errors (§16.3). Null for errors that do not come from text. |
| `metadata` | `record` | — | required | Error-specific structured detail — the exit status of an external process, the signal name, the candidate list of an ambiguous name. An empty record when there is none. |

## File — `ono.file/1`

A filesystem object and its metadata.

Identity: `device`, `inode`

Default view: `name`, `kind`, `size`, `modified`, `owner`

| field | type | unit | presence | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | `path` | — | required | The path this record was reached by. A reference, not an identity — hard links share one inode. |
| `name` | `string` | — | required | The final component of the path. |
| `kind` | `enum` | — | required | The object kind, exactly as spec §28.2 enumerates it. |
| `size` | `bytesize` | — | nullable | Apparent size in bytes; null for kinds where size is not meaningful or not readable. |
| `owner` | `ref<ono.user/1>` | — | nullable | Owning user; carries the numeric uid even when the name cannot be resolved. |
| `group` | `ref<ono.group/1>` | — | nullable | Owning group; carries the numeric gid even when the name cannot be resolved. |
| `mode` | `string` | — | nullable | Permission bits with the setuid/setgid/sticky flags, as four octal digits, e.g. "0644". A string rather than an int because the grammar has no octal literal to compare against (ADR-0009); a `PermissionMode` semantic scalar is deferred, see ADR-0012. |
| `modified` | `timestamp` | — | nullable | Last content modification time. |
| `accessed` | `timestamp` | — | nullable | Last access time; null on filesystems mounted without access-time tracking. |
| `created` | `timestamp` | — | nullable | Creation time; null on filesystems that do not record it. |
| `inode` | `int` | — | nullable | Inode number; null where the filesystem has no inode concept. |
| `device` | `ref<ono.device/1>` | — | nullable | The device the object lives on. |
| `target` | `path` | — | nullable | The symlink target; null for every kind other than `symlink`. |

## Filesystem — `ono.filesystem/1`

A filesystem and its capacity, mounted or not.

Identity: `uuid`, `source`

Default view: `source`, `type`, `size`, `used`, `available`, `target`

| field | type | unit | presence | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `source` | `string` | — | required | The backing device or source. A string, because a network filesystem's source is not a path. |
| `type` | `string` | — | required | The filesystem type as the system names it. |
| `uuid` | `uuid` | — | nullable | The filesystem UUID; null for types that carry none. The stable half of the identity. |
| `label` | `string` | — | nullable | The filesystem label; null when unlabelled. |
| `target` | `path` | — | nullable | The mount point, or null when the filesystem is not currently mounted. |
| `size` | `bytesize` | — | nullable | Total capacity; null when the filesystem is not mounted or reports none. |
| `used` | `bytesize` | — | nullable | Space in use. |
| `available` | `bytesize` | — | nullable | Space available to this user. Distinct from `size - used`, because reserved blocks are counted as used space nobody unprivileged can have. |
| `read_only` | `bool` | — | nullable | Whether the filesystem is currently mounted read-only; null when not mounted. |
| `device` | `ref<ono.device/1>` | — | nullable | The backing device; null for network and pseudo-filesystems. |

## GraphEdge — `ono.graph-edge/1`

One relationship between two objects in a graph.

Identity: 

Default view: `from`, `relation`, `to`, `confidence`, `provider`

| field | type | unit | presence | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `from` | `value` | — | required | The reference of the source node. |
| `to` | `value` | — | required | The reference of the target node. |
| `relation` | `string` | — | required | The relationship name, e.g. `owns`, `listens`, `reads`, `requires` (spec §22.4). |
| `direction` | `enum` | — | required | Whether the relationship runs from `from` to `to`, or holds symmetrically. |
| `confidence` | `enum` | — | required | Whether the provider observed the relationship or derived it. Required, never defaulted: spec §22.2 forbids presenting an inference as an observation. |
| `provider` | `string` | — | required | Which provider asserted the edge, so a questionable relationship can be traced to its source. |
| `metadata` | `record` | — | required | Relationship-specific detail, such as the file descriptor or the socket inode; empty when there is none. |

## GraphNode — `ono.graph-node/1`

One object in a relationship graph.

Identity: 

Default view: `id`, `kind`

| field | type | unit | presence | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | `value` | — | required | A reference to the object this node stands for; unique within the graph. |
| `kind` | `string` | — | required | The schema id of the object, e.g. `ono.process/1`, so a renderer can label it. |
| `value` | `record` | — | required | A summary of the object's fields — enough to render a row without a second query, not the whole record. |

## Graph — `ono.graph/1`

A relationship graph over system objects, as produced by `trace`.

Identity: 

Default view: `root`, `nodes`, `edges`

| field | type | unit | presence | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `root` | `value` | — | nullable | The object the trace started from, so a renderer can lay the graph out from it. Null for a graph with no distinguished origin. |
| `nodes` | `list<ono.graph-node/1>` | — | required | Every object in the graph, each appearing exactly once. |
| `edges` | `list<ono.graph-edge/1>` | — | required | The relationships between the nodes. |

## Group — `ono.group/1`

A group account.

Identity: `gid`

Default view: `gid`, `name`, `members`

| field | type | unit | presence | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `gid` | `int` | — | required | The numeric group id. Always present, even when no name resolves for it. |
| `name` | `string` | — | nullable | The group name; null when the identity provider cannot resolve the gid. |
| `members` | `list<string>` | — | nullable | Login names listed as supplementary members. Names rather than user references, because the account database stores names and they need not resolve to an account. Users whose primary group this is are not listed here; null when the provider cannot enumerate them. |

## Interface — `ono.interface/1`

A network interface with its addresses, operational state and counters.

Identity: `index`

Default view: `name`, `state`, `addresses`, `mtu`, `mac`

| field | type | unit | presence | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | — | required | The interface name. Renameable, so a reference but not the identity. |
| `index` | `int` | — | required | The kernel interface index. |
| `mac` | `string` | — | nullable | The link-layer address; null for interfaces that have none, such as loopback or tun. |
| `state` | `enum` | — | required | The operational state as the kernel reports it, not the administrative flag. |
| `mtu` | `int` | — | required | The maximum transmission unit in bytes. |
| `addresses` | `list<ipnetwork>` | — | required | Configured addresses with their prefix lengths; an empty list when none are configured. |
| `rx_bytes` | `bytesize` | — | nullable | Bytes received since the counter was last reset; null when the provider has no counters. |
| `tx_bytes` | `bytesize` | — | nullable | Bytes transmitted since the counter was last reset. |

## Job — `ono.job/1`

A backgrounded pipeline — an external process group, or a detached native live view.

Identity: `id`

Default view: `id`, `state`, `kind`, `command`, `started`

| field | type | unit | presence | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | `int` | — | required | The job number, the `+1` the prompt shows (§18.4). Unique within the session. |
| `kind` | `enum` | — | required | Whether the job is an external process group under classic job control (§18.1) or a detached native live stream (§18.4). They are cancelled by different mechanisms (§18.5). |
| `state` | `enum` | — | required | The job's current state. |
| `command` | `string` | — | required | The source text of the pipeline, as typed, so the job list is readable. |
| `current` | `bool` | — | required | Whether this is the job an unqualified job reference resolves to. |
| `process_group` | `int` | — | nullable | The process group id; null for a native job, which owns no process group. |
| `pids` | `list<int>` | — | nullable | The process ids in the job; null for a native job. |
| `started` | `timestamp` | — | required | When the job was detached. |
| `exit_status` | `int` | — | nullable | The exit status once the job finished; null while it is still running. A job terminated by a signal reports its status through the `external.signal` error, not as a fabricated number. |

## Mount — `ono.mount/1`

A mounted filesystem, with its options kept as data rather than as one option string.

Identity: `target`

Default view: `target`, `source`, `filesystem`, `read_only`

| field | type | unit | presence | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `source` | `string` | — | required | What is mounted — a device path, a network location, or a pseudo-filesystem name. A string, not a path, because it is not always one. |
| `target` | `path` | — | required | The mount point. |
| `filesystem` | `string` | — | required | The filesystem type as the kernel names it. |
| `options` | `list<string>` | — | required | The mount options, one element per option, never a single joined string. |
| `read_only` | `bool` | — | required | Whether the mount is read-only. Extracted from the options because users filter on it. |
| `device` | `ref<ono.device/1>` | — | nullable | The backing device; null for pseudo- and network filesystems. |

## Neighbor — `ono.neighbor/1`

An ARP or NDP neighbour table entry.

Identity: `address`, `interface`

Default view: `address`, `mac`, `interface`, `state`

| field | type | unit | presence | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `address` | `ip` | — | required | The neighbour's network address. |
| `mac` | `string` | — | nullable | The resolved link-layer address; null for an incomplete or failed entry. Null here means "not resolved", which is exactly what spec §10.5 requires it to mean. |
| `interface` | `ref<ono.interface/1>` | — | required | The interface the neighbour was seen on; part of the identity, since addresses repeat. |
| `family` | `enum` | — | required | The address family. |
| `state` | `enum` | — | required | The neighbour cache state as the kernel reports it. |
| `router` | `bool` | — | nullable | Whether the neighbour advertises itself as a router; null outside NDP. |
| `updated` | `timestamp` | — | nullable | When the entry was last confirmed; null when the provider keeps no timestamp. |

## Process — `ono.process/1`

A running process as the process provider observes it.

Identity: `pid`, `started`

Default view: `pid`, `name`, `cpu`, `memory`, `user`

| field | type | unit | presence | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pid` | `int` | — | required | The process id. |
| `ppid` | `int` | — | nullable | The parent process id; null for the init process and when the parent is not visible. |
| `name` | `string` | — | required | The short process name, as the kernel records it. |
| `command` | `list<string>` | — | nullable | The full argument vector; null when the process hides it or it is not readable. |
| `executable` | `path` | — | nullable | The resolved executable path; null when the link is unreadable or the file is deleted. |
| `user` | `ref<ono.user/1>` | — | nullable | The effective user; carries the numeric uid even when the name cannot be resolved. |
| `group` | `ref<ono.group/1>` | — | nullable | The effective group; carries the numeric gid even when the name cannot be resolved. |
| `state` | `enum` | — | required | The kernel scheduling state. `unknown` when the provider read a state it does not model. |
| `cpu` | `float` | percent | nullable | Share of one logical CPU, as spec §28.1 documents it. Null until a second sample exists, because a single procfs read cannot answer it. |
| `memory` | `bytesize` | — | nullable | Resident set size. |
| `virtual_mem` | `bytesize` | — | nullable | Virtual memory size. |
| `threads` | `int` | — | nullable | Number of threads in the process. |
| `started` | `timestamp` | — | nullable | Wall-clock start time. Part of the identity, so a provider that cannot answer it yields a process whose identity is pid alone and is therefore vulnerable to pid reuse. |
| `cwd` | `path` | — | nullable | Current working directory; null when not readable by this user. |
| `service` | `ref<ono.service/1>` | — | nullable | The service unit the process belongs to; null when it belongs to none. |
| `container` | `ref<ono.container/1>` | — | nullable | The container the process runs in; null outside a container or without a provider. |

## Route — `ono.route/1`

A routing table entry.

Identity: `table`, `family`, `destination`, `gateway`, `interface`

Default view: `destination`, `gateway`, `interface`, `metric`, `protocol`

| field | type | unit | presence | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `destination` | `ipnetwork` | — | nullable | The destination prefix. Null is the default route — a real answer, not an unknown one. |
| `gateway` | `ip` | — | nullable | The next hop; null for a directly connected route. |
| `interface` | `ref<ono.interface/1>` | — | nullable | The outgoing interface; null for routes that name none, such as blackholes. |
| `source` | `ip` | — | nullable | The preferred source address for traffic taking this route. |
| `family` | `enum` | — | required | The address family of the route. |
| `type` | `enum` | — | nullable | The route type; null when the provider does not distinguish types. |
| `scope` | `enum` | — | nullable | The scope of the destination. |
| `protocol` | `string` | — | nullable | What installed the route — `kernel`, `static`, `dhcp`, `ra`, a routing daemon's name. A string because the set is the system's registry of route origins, not Ono's. |
| `metric` | `int` | — | nullable | The route priority; lower wins. Null when the provider supplies no metric. |
| `table` | `string` | — | nullable | The routing table the entry belongs to, by name where one exists, otherwise its number. |

## Service — `ono.service/1`

A service-manager unit as the active service provider sees it.

Identity: `provider`, `name`

Default view: `name`, `state`, `substate`, `enabled`, `description`

| field | type | unit | presence | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | — | required | The unit name, including its suffix where the provider uses one. |
| `description` | `string` | — | nullable | The human description the unit declares. |
| `state` | `enum` | — | required | The high-level activity state. |
| `substate` | `string` | — | nullable | The provider-specific sub-state (`running`, `exited`, `dead`, …). A string rather than an enum because the set is the provider's, not Ono's. |
| `pid` | `int` | — | nullable | The main process id; null when the unit runs no process or it is not visible. |
| `enabled` | `bool` | — | nullable | Whether the unit starts at boot; null when the provider has no such concept. |
| `since` | `timestamp` | — | nullable | When the unit entered its current state. |
| `provider` | `string` | — | required | The service provider that produced this record; part of the identity. |
| `unit_file` | `path` | — | nullable | The unit file backing the service; null for transient or generated units. |

## Socket — `ono.socket/1`

A socket with its endpoints, owner and state.

Identity: `inode`

Default view: `protocol`, `local`, `remote`, `state`, `process`

| field | type | unit | presence | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `protocol` | `enum` | — | required | The transport protocol. |
| `family` | `enum` | — | required | The address family. |
| `local` | `ono.endpoint/1` | — | nullable | The local endpoint; null for socket kinds that have none. |
| `remote` | `ono.endpoint/1` | — | nullable | The peer endpoint; null for listening and connectionless sockets. |
| `state` | `enum` | — | nullable | The connection state; null for protocols that have none, such as UDP. |
| `process` | `ref<ono.process/1>` | — | nullable | The owning process; null when no process owns the socket, or when this user may not see the owner. Spec §10.5 forbids collapsing those two into an empty string. |
| `user` | `ref<ono.user/1>` | — | nullable | The owning user. |
| `inode` | `int` | — | nullable | The socket inode; the identity field, null when the provider cannot supply it. |

## User — `ono.user/1`

A user account.

Identity: `uid`

Default view: `uid`, `name`, `home`, `shell`

| field | type | unit | presence | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `uid` | `int` | — | required | The numeric user id. Always present, even when no name resolves for it. |
| `name` | `string` | — | nullable | The login name; null when the identity provider cannot resolve the uid. |
| `primary_group` | `ref<ono.group/1>` | — | nullable | The primary group. |
| `home` | `path` | — | nullable | The home directory as the account database records it; not checked for existence. |
| `shell` | `path` | — | nullable | The login shell as the account database records it. |
| `gecos` | `string` | — | nullable | The GECOS field, unparsed. |
